text: The chapter notes that one two-input connective is *functionally complete* — every Boolean function can be built from it alone. Which one?
explanation: NAND (the Sheffer stroke) is functionally complete: every Boolean function is expressible using NAND alone, which is why NAND gates are the universal building block of digital circuits. None of →, ↔, or ∧ is complete by itself — each maps all-true inputs to true, so none can even express ¬.
